findings.finding: The street's FY26 ex-refund EPS of $8.43 (Earnings Whispers) sits $0.32 below the company's own ex-refund guide midpoint of $8.75 ($9.90-10.90 less ~$1.65); with YTD ex-refund EPS $4.18 and Q3 consensus $2.03, the street implies Q4 ~$2.22 against $2.44 a year ago, while the guide midpoint implies Q4 ~$2.40-2.54 - so merely holding the range lifts Q4 estimates, and street revenue (~$108.7B) is also below the ~$110B guide.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q2 2026 guide raise (+$0.75 at midpoint ex-refund) bought +4.28%; the Nov 2025 print, where the guide was not raised, fell -2.77% (baseline).
findings.why_not_priced: If the market held the guide midpoint the published FY consensus would sit near $8.75, not $8.43; the gap is visible in the street's own numbers. The buy-side may already be higher (RBC sees the upper end, whisper $2.17), so part is priced in the whisper rather than the consensus.
findings.independence: Company guide in the Q2 release (https://corporate.target.com/press/release/2026/08/target-corporation-reports-second-quarter-earnings); RBC's upper-end FY view (https://finimize.com/content/rbc-sees-walmart-steady-and-target-beating-estimates). Street $8.43 is single-sourced.

findings.finding: Two brokers model Q3 comps at +4% against a ~+3.4% consensus: RBC (EPS $2.25 vs $2.06 expected, FY toward the upper end of $9.90-10.90) and BofA (comp forecast raised to 4%, although EPS cut to $2.08).
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q2 comps +3.8% vs lower expectations with a raise: +4.28%; earlier comp beats were not consistently paid (3 of last 8 prints up).
findings.source_date: 2026-11 (undated page; references the 2026-11-18 report and the $9.90-10.90 range)
findings.why_not_priced: Published notes are on the wire, so mostly priced into the whisper; the comp above consensus is what moves the reported line if it lands.
findings.independence: BofA preview, different broker, same comp view: https://finimize.com/content/target-heads-into-q3-with-strong-sales-and-tighter-margins

findings.finding: The real bar is above consensus: whisper $2.17 is ~7% over the $2.03 consensus and the Earnings Whispers preview says an in-line quarter could disappoint, with sentiment 'still bullish, though a bit cooler'; RBC sits at $2.25.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Nov 2025 print (EPS ahead of consensus) fell -2.77%; 5 of last 8 prints fell (baseline).
findings.why_not_priced: Consensus-based screens show a ~14% EPS growth bar; the market's operative bar is the whisper. If the stock were pricing only consensus, the whisper would sit near $2.03.

findings.finding: Q3 laps an easy compare: Q3 2025 comps -2.7% and adjusted EPS $1.78, while Q2 2026 printed comps +3.8% on +3.6% traffic and ex-refund EPS $2.46 (about +20%), so a consensus beat is the base case.
findings.why_not_priced: Largely priced; consensus already assumes +14% EPS growth. Filed because a beat is the base case the judges should anchor on, sized small.

findings.finding: Supplier Mattel cut its 2026 outlook in early November 2026 (constant-currency sales +1% to +4%, adj EPS $1.05-1.20), citing softer-than-expected POS and a late-Q3 deceleration that continued into Q4 across major markets, plus retailer orders shifting into Q4.
findings.link: Mattel sells toys through US mass retailers; Target is one of its largest customers alongside Walmart and Amazon, and toys/'Fun101' are among Target's named growth categories and a core holiday category; Target-specific share of Mattel revenue not sourced.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Holiday-guide tone: Nov 2025 print with cautious holiday outlook -2.77%; Nov 2024 (outside the baseline's 8) is not cited.
findings.why_not_priced: Retail previews on TGT focus on Q3 comps and margins; none cite supplier POS. If priced, the TGT whisper would have come down after Nov 5 rather than standing $0.14 above consensus.
findings.independence: Bank of America card data: discretionary growth cooled in October (https://institute.bankofamerica.com/economic-insights/consumer-checkpoint-november-2026.html). Mattel page itself was bot-blocked; content via search summary.

findings.finding: On 2026-09-29 (mid-quarter) Target cut prices on nearly 2,000 home, apparel and accessories items, some apparel 20%+ below last year and bedding ~15% lower, on top of 10,000+ cuts over the past year - margin pressure in its highest-margin, still-flat categories; BofA cut Q3 EPS to $2.08 on promotions, freight and SG&A.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Gross-margin line: Q2 ex-refund GM +~100bp helped the +4.28% reaction; margin was the swing factor in prior negative prints (2025-05 -5.21%, 2025-08 -6.33%).
findings.why_not_priced: The cut was a public Reuters story, so partly priced; its margin cost lands in the Q3/Q4 gross margin that consensus at $2.03 may or may not include. Net of the rest of the company: food, beauty and Fun101 (the growth categories) are not affected, so sized small.

findings.finding: Placer.ai: Target visits on its October deal days (Oct 6-9, 2026, against Amazon's Prime Big Deal Days) were up 6.0% year over year and +2.1% against the Aug 31-Oct 4 baseline - traffic momentum continuing into the last month of Q3.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Traffic-led comp (+3.6% traffic) in Q2 bought +4.28%.
findings.why_not_priced: One week of foot traffic is a narrow proxy and is public; it supports the 4% comp view rather than adding to it. Proxy, sized small.

findings.finding: Bank of America card data: October 2026 spending per household +5.8% YoY (+4.6% ex-gas), but growth cooled across a number of discretionary categories, average ticket falling and consumers more price-conscious; higher gas prices tied to the Middle East conflict.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: No direct history; holiday-tone guides moved the stock in Nov 2025 (-2.77%).
findings.why_not_priced: Public macro series, mostly priced; filed as a proxy for discretionary softness heading into the holiday guide.
findings.independence: Mattel late-Q3/Q4 deceleration (counterparty) points the same way; NRF Retail Monitor says October was a 13th straight month of gains (opposite).

findings.finding: Home Depot reported Q3 FY2026 on 2026-11-17: sales $43.4B (+4.9%), comps +2.2% (US +2.2%), adjusted EPS $3.86 vs $3.74 a year ago, with a fiscal 2026 guidance update.
findings.link: none stated (overlapping US consumer and home category; no quantified shared-channel figure)
findings.why_not_priced: Released this morning, already in the TGT close; weak link, sized near zero.

findings.finding: Further IEEPA tariff refunds may land in Q3: the CFO said Q2's $994M refund was the 'significant majority' of refunds applied for to date but more are expected, guidance excludes them, and CBP's CAPE Phase 3 opened 2026-10-06; any Q3 refund would lift GAAP/adjusted EPS and the headline FY range mechanically.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q2 refund quarter +4.28%, but the move rode the ex-refund beat and raise; Walmart fell ~10% on a refund-flattered Q2 (https://www.tikr.com/blog/walmart-fell-10-after-its-last-report-is-it-time-to-sell-before-november-19-or-load-up).
findings.why_not_priced: Size and timing unknown and management tells investors to look through refunds; a headline beat from refunds could confuse the first prints of the session but should be stripped by the close.

findings.finding: Management said on the Q2 call it expected capacity to resume share repurchases in the second half (subject to performance, cash and ratings), funded in part by the ~$994M refund cash; Q3 is the first quarter where a resumption can show.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: No resumption on record in the baseline window.
findings.why_not_priced: Flagged publicly as 'a signal to watch' (Earnings Whispers); a resumed buyback with a sized program would be new, an absence would be read as caution.
findings.independence: Earnings Whispers preview names buyback resumption as a watch item (https://www.earningswhispers.com/article/TGT/23131).

findings.finding: The stock has not run into the print: -0.9% since the 2026-08-19 post-print close, -7.2% off the 2026-08-24 high, 20d +2.8% vs XRT +2.1%, 5d -2.6% vs XRT -4.1% - roughly in line with retail, contradicting the '+12% since last report' framing in the preview.
findings.why_not_priced: A stock priced for a blowout would have run versus XRT into the print; it has not, so the price is not stretched even though the whisper is elevated.
